context:
Treat compatibility pruning as data, not control-flow folklore. Reuse the
existing SQL compatibility registry if it can represent platform/benchmark
gates cleanly; otherwise add the smallest dedicated UAT compatibility layer
and document why the SQL registry was not a good fit.
description:
The 2026-05-12 enabled-platform run enumerated a broad set of enabled-platform
cells but did not provide durable accounting for "all possible benchmarks" by
platform. The local enumeration path reports 57 candidate cells per platform
across 22 public benchmarks and three scale rungs, while the observed
`matrix_summary.tsv` contains 96 executed cells because early failure
behavior and scale filtering stopped many candidates before execution.

UAT needs a first-class compatibility gate: every benchmark excluded for a
platform must have an explicit rule id, source evidence, and justification.
Everything else must run, and the report must distinguish executed, passed,
failed, timed out, compatibility-pruned, and ladder-pruned cells.

anti_patterns.dont: count early-stop-pruned cells as passed, failed, or compatibility-pruned
hard-code a list of benchmarks to skip inside `enumerate.py` without rule ids and source evidence
let the enabled-platform coverage sweep silently stop after the first failure on a platform

work_units.notes:
Re-run or script the enumeration for `lakesail`, `pg-duckdb`,
`pg-mooncake`, and `timescaledb` on the current branch, and compare it to
the 2026-05-12 artifact counts. Commit only a compact summary if durable
evidence is needed; keep raw enumeration output under `/tmp` or
`BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR`.

Current coverage-sweep config
`tests/uat/configs/uat-enabled-platforms-enumeration.yaml` enumerates
88 executable cells and 0 compatibility-pruned cells for `lakesail`,
`pg-duckdb`, `pg-mooncake`, and `timescaledb` at SF=0.01 across all
public benchmarks. The prior broad run's 96 executed rows reflected a
different multi-rung config plus early-stop behavior, not a durable
compatibility policy.
work_units.summary: Recompute current candidate and observed cell accounting

work_units.notes:
Add or extend a registry-backed rule model for platform/benchmark
compatibility. A rule must include platform, benchmark, rule id, status
such as `blocked` or `experimental`, a human-readable reason, and source
evidence. Prefer reusing SQL compatibility registry patterns before
adding a new convention.

Added UAT-local compatibility rules in `tests/uat/compatibility.py`.
This deliberately avoids coupling runtime `benchbox.sql_compat` to
UAT-only run policy. Rules expose `rule_id`, `status`, `reason`, and
`evidence`; the first rule covers dataframe platforms paired with
SQL-only benchmarks.
work_units.summary: Define the platform-benchmark compatibility data model

work_units.notes:
Update enumeration so compatibility-pruned cells are emitted with reasons
and not silently dropped. Update matrix/report outputs to show candidate,
executed, compatibility-pruned, early-stop-pruned, passed, failed, and
timed-out counts per platform and benchmark.

`enumerate_cells_with_pruning()` now returns executable cells plus
compatibility-pruned cells. The orchestrator writes
`compatibility_pruned.jsonl`, and report footers include candidate,
executed, compatibility-pruned, early-stop-pruned, passed, failed, and
timed-out counts.
work_units.summary: Apply compatibility rules during UAT enumeration and reporting

work_units.notes:
The enabled-platform UAT config must be able to run all non-blocked
benchmarks for each enabled platform. If early-stop behavior remains for
short developer smoke runs, it must be disabled or separately accounted
for in coverage sweeps.

Added `tests/uat/configs/uat-enabled-platforms-enumeration.yaml` for the
enabled-platform coverage-sweep shape. It sets `early_stop_on_failure:
false` and a high `early_stop_after_s` so non-blocked cells are attempted
rather than ladder-pruned in coverage runs.
work_units.summary: Add coverage-sweep mode that attempts every non-blocked cell

work_units.notes:

Updated `docs/operations/uat-framework.md` with the UAT compatibility

work_units.summary: Document the rule format and update existing UAT docs
